_doc: Unit 1 practice questions: the ONE place these are written. tools/build-practice-script.ts turns this into script/u1-practice.md (spoken), src/episodes/u1-practice.ts reads it for the cards, tools/export-quiz.ts turns it into a quiz CSV + answer key. Spoken text (ask/answer/why) is linted like any script; facts must cite registry ids.
title: Unit 1 Practice
intro: Unit 1 practice. Three exam-style questions, mixed across the unit. Say your answer out loud before we give it.
outro: That's the set. If one tripped you up, rewatch that episode, then come back and try again.

questions.ask: Question one. It's a stimulus. A Nahua account in the Florentine Codex describes smallpox victims lying in their homes, unable to move, with no one left to care for them. What larger pattern does it illustrate?

card.stem: What larger pattern does this account illustrate?

source.title: FLORENTINE CODEX, BOOK 12 (PARAPHRASED)
source.text: Smallpox victims lay in their homes, unable to move, with no one left to care for them.

questions.prompt: A Nahua account: smallpox victims unable to move, no one left to care for them. What larger pattern?
questions.answer: A virgin-soil epidemic: Old World diseases hitting people with no prior exposure, emptying towns ahead of the soldiers.
questions.reveal: A virgin-soil epidemic. Disease ran ahead of the conquest.
questions.why: Name the pattern, then use the source. And notice it was compiled decades later, under a Spanish friar. That's a sourcing point.

questions.ask: Question two. A historian argues the potato did more to change Europe than any treaty of the 1500s. Defend or refute, using the Exchange.

card.stem: “The potato did more to change Europe than any treaty of the 1500s.” Defend or refute, using the Exchange.

questions.prompt: Did the potato change Europe more than any treaty of the 1500s? Defend or refute.
questions.answer: Defend it, and you'd say new crops reshaped populations: the potato helped fuel Europe's boom, and maize did the same in Africa and Asia. Refute it, and you'd argue silver and empire mattered more.
questions.reveal: Defend: new crops fueled population growth. Either way, bring evidence.
questions.why: Either side can score. What earns the point is a clear claim plus specific evidence from the Exchange.

questions.ask: Question three. Native labor collapses, and the sugar plantations still need workers. Where had Europeans already used enslaved African labor on sugar, and what happened next?

card.stem: Where had Europeans already used enslaved African labor on sugar, and what happened next?

questions.prompt: Where had Europeans already used enslaved African labor on sugar? What happened next?
questions.answer: Madeira and São Tomé. Then the model crossed the Atlantic, and the Middle Passage carried enslaved Africans by the millions.
questions.reveal: Madeira and São Tomé. The model crossed to the Americas.
questions.why: Causation questions want the chain: the labor collapse, the island model, then the Atlantic trade.
